## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `co-mutation-cohort-inference`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-31T06:12:41.171Z.

Catalog entry, by slug: co-mutation-cohort-inference

Recorded 2026-07-31. Extends the catalog; no prior entry is renumbered or restated. Owner recorded on the algorithm portfolio registry.

The corpus shape this exists for. Measured on this tracker today: every one of 2,226 nodes reaches an outcome milestone through a typed non-related path within five hops, and 1,839 of 2,096 ordered nodes — 87.7 percent — have no predecessor at all. The graph is reachability-saturated and order-starved. Two consequences follow for any assembler that ranks candidates. Graph distance to an outcome is nearly uninformative, because almost everything is one to three hops away. Ordering position is unavailable, because almost nothing has one. The two structural signals the engine would naturally reach for are both degenerate on the shape this corpus actually has, and there is good reason to expect that shape to be typical rather than exceptional: ordering edges must be authored, and authoring them is exactly the work that gets skipped under delivery pressure.

The observation the entry exploits. Ordering was never authored, but it was recorded. Every mutation appends a history entry carrying a timestamp, an author identity, and — since harness detection shipped — an agent instance identifier. Work that was actually done together leaves a trace of having been done together, in a stream that is append-only, hash-chained, and can never be back-written. That trace is available for the entire corpus including terminal items, and reading it requires no write to any item, which matters because writes to terminal items currently re-bucket the changelog.

The algorithm. Treat the union of history streams as a sequence of mutation events, each a triple of item id, timestamp, and actor key, where the actor key is the agent instance when present and falls back to the author identity. Partition the event sequence per actor into sessions by a gap threshold: consecutive events by one actor separated by less than the threshold belong to one session. Each session yields a cohort, the set of distinct item ids it touched. Cohort membership is the raw signal.

Score it as a similarity rather than an edge. For a pair of items, define co-mutation affinity as the sum over shared cohorts of an inverse-size weight — one over the logarithm of cohort size, so a session that touched four items is strong evidence of relatedness and a bulk pass that touched nine hundred is nearly none — multiplied by a recency decay on the session timestamp. This is the same intuition that makes inverse document frequency work and it is essential here, because this project's history contains large mechanical backfills whose cohorts would otherwise dominate every score.

Fold it into assembly as a query-conditioned term. Given a seed set — the claimed item, the item named in the request, or the items already selected by the packer — the co-mutation term for a candidate is its affinity summed against the seed set. Add it to the existing relevance score alongside metadata, graph position, recency and usage affinity. Attach the strongest contributing session to the candidate as its explanation, so a candidate never enters the context window on this signal without being able to say which recorded work session links it to the seed.

Why it is a substitute for the missing ordering rather than a duplicate of the existing graph term. The graph term answers what is structurally connected to this. The co-mutation term answers what was actually being worked on when this was being worked on, which is a different question and the one an agent resuming a task is really asking. On a corpus with a rich authored ordering the two largely agree, and the term contributes little beyond confirmation. On a corpus with no authored ordering — the common case, and this corpus — it is the only available evidence of temporal association, and it is derived from the one channel that cannot be forged.

Cost and scale, which is where most retrieval signals fail. Cohorts are computed by a single ordered pass over the event stream, so construction is linear in events and requires no random access. The output is a sparse item-to-cohort posting list, which is the same data structure the search index already maintains, so scoring a candidate against a seed set is a posting-list intersection bounded by the number of cohorts the seed touched rather than by corpus size. Cohorts older than the retention horizon are folded into a decayed summary and their per-item detail dropped, so the structure is bounded in the number of live cohorts rather than in the number of historical events — a decade-long corpus costs what a month-long corpus costs, at lower resolution for the distant past. The construction pass is incremental: new events extend the newest cohorts and never revisit old ones.

Required degeneracies, which are the acceptance conditions and also the falsifier.

On a workspace of a few items and a few minutes, every event falls in one session, so every cohort is the whole workspace, so the inverse-size weight drives every affinity to approximately zero and the term contributes nothing. The small end must pay no ranking distortion and no measurable latency for machinery it cannot use.

On a single-author corpus the actor partition is trivial and the signal reduces to pure temporal adjacency, which is weaker but still correct. It must not be silently stronger — a single actor is not evidence of coordination.

On a corpus with a fully authored ordering, the term must not override it. Ordering edges are asserted facts and co-mutation is inferred association; where they disagree, the assertion wins and the disagreement is surfaced rather than resolved, which is the composition rule the cross-channel-disagreement entry already establishes.

Under a token budget the explanations degrade before the candidates, consistent with every other entry in this catalog.

Bulk mechanical passes must be visible as such. A session that touched a thousand items in ninety seconds is a migration, not collaboration. The inverse-size weight handles this continuously, but the acceptance test should assert it explicitly: a synthetic backfill cohort must not raise any pair's affinity above the floor.

The falsifier. Run the assembler with the term enabled and disabled against the graded judgment corpus. If the term changes no ranking on a corpus with authored ordering, it is redundant and belongs behind a shape condition rather than in the default path. If it changes rankings on the small-workspace fixture at all, the degeneracy is broken and the entry is not adoptable as specified.

What this entry is not. It is not the usage-affinity signal, which learns from what was served and acted on; this learns from what was written, which exists for the entire historical corpus rather than only for the period since serving was instrumented. It is not the trajectory projection feature, which produces an ordered observation-action-outcome artifact for training and offline evaluation; this consumes the same stream to produce a retrieval signal, and the two should share one pass over history rather than each making their own. It is not the ordering-evidence tranche, which recovers asserted prerequisite edges from item text and writes them; this asserts nothing and writes nothing. And it is explicitly not a replacement for authoring ordering — it is what makes the engine useful during the years in which ordering remains mostly unauthored, which on the measured evidence is the normal state of a real project.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
